prompts.L1:

Surrounded by bone, surrounded by cells, by rings, by rings of hell, by hair, surrounded by air-is-a-thing, surrounded by silhouette, by honey-wet bees, yet by skeletons of trees, surrounded by actual, yes, for practical purposes, people, surrounded by surreal popcorn, surrounded by the reborn: Surrender in the center to surroundings. O surrender forever, never end her, let her blend around, surrender to the surroundings that surround the tender endo-surrender, that tumble through the tumbling to that blue that curls around the crumbling, to that, the blue that rumbles under the sun bounding the pearl that we walk on, talk on; we can chalk that up to experience, sensing the brown here that’s blue now, a drop of water surrounding a cow that’s black & white, the warbling Blackburnian twitter that’s machining midnight orange in the light that’s glittering in the light green visible wind. That’s the ticket to the tunnel through the thicket that’s a cricket’s funnel of music to correct & pick it out from under the wing that whirls up over & out.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Surrounded, Surrender, Blackburnian

outputs.L1:
Surrounded by bone, by cells, by rings—by rings of hell—by hair; surrounded by air-is-a-thing, by silhouette, by honey-wet bees, and yet by skeletons of trees; surrounded by actual—yes, for practical purposes—people; surrounded by surreal popcorn, surrounded by the reborn: surrender, at the center, to the surroundings.

O surrender forever; never end her. Let her blend around. Surrender to the surroundings that surround the tender endo-surrender, tumbling through the tumbling toward that blue which curls around the crumbling—that blue which rumbles beneath the sun, bounding the pearl we walk on, talk on. We can chalk that up to experience: sensing the brown here that is blue now, a drop of water surrounding a cow that is black and white; the warbling Blackburnian twitter machining midnight orange in the light that glitters through the light-green, visible wind. That is the ticket to the tunnel through the thicket—a cricket’s funnel of music—to correct and pick it out from beneath the wing that whirls up, over, and out.
outputs.L2: Encased in bone and enclosed by cells, within circles upon circles of torment, among hair and the tangible substance of air, bordered by outlines, bees damp with honey, and the bare frameworks of trees—hemmed in, too, by real people, at least in every practical sense, as well as dreamlike popcorn and those born anew—yield at the core to everything around you. Give way endlessly; do not bring her to an ending, but allow her to dissolve into what encloses her. Submit to the environment embracing the delicate inward surrender, carried through repeated falling toward the blue that coils around decay: the blue reverberating beneath the sun and enclosing this pearl where we walk and speak. Call it something learned through experience: feeling the brown of this place become blue, like one bead of water encircling a black-and-white cow, while the rippling call of a Blackburnian bird manufactures midnight orange amid sparkling light and a pale-green wind that can be seen. That sound provides passage into the tunnel cutting through the brush—a cricket’s narrowing channel of music, enabling us to identify and extract it from beneath the wing as it spirals upward, across, and away.
outputs.L3:
The speaker portrays existence as enclosed within overlapping layers of nature, physical bodies, everyday objects, and surreal imagery. These elements do not form a stable or orderly landscape; instead, they crowd together and flow into one another, creating a world that feels both tangled and alive. At the center of this dense environment, the poem calls for a complete and unending surrender to the world. Rather than resisting the confusion of experience, the individual is urged to enter it fully and allow the boundaries of the self to weaken.

Through this surrender, personal identity begins to dissolve into the movement, color, and texture of the surrounding environment. A series of shifting sensory images links earth and sky, water and wind, animals and birdsong, light and matter. These connections suggest that every part of existence participates in a larger, continuously changing whole. Surrender is therefore not presented as passive defeat, but as a form of intense attention and openness. By yielding to the world’s complexity, the individual becomes capable of perceiving distinct meanings, rhythms, and music within what initially appears to be an overwhelming tangle.
outputs.L4:
The poem explores the relationship between the self and the surrounding world as a process of immersion rather than separation. Instead of presenting identity as fixed, stable, or self-contained, it portrays the speaker as moving through a reality that continually enters, alters, and exceeds the individual consciousness. The boundaries between inner experience and external nature gradually dissolve: sensations, objects, sounds, and thoughts flow into one another until the self becomes part of a larger, interconnected field of perception.

This movement is reflected in the poem’s form. Cascading repetitions create momentum, allowing words and images to accumulate, return, and change meaning through their recurrence. The language does not advance in a straightforward logical sequence; it develops associatively, through echoes, puns, unexpected juxtapositions, and shifts between the senses. Sounds may acquire color or texture, while visible objects may seem to speak, move, or become musical. Such surreal transformations suggest that reality is not passively observed but actively remade by attention and imagination.

At first, this abundance may appear chaotic. The poem’s rapidly changing images and verbal turns resist any single, stable interpretation. Yet the apparent disorder is also the source of its vitality. By relinquishing the desire to control or organize everything around a central “I,” the speaker discovers a different kind of freedom. Surrender does not mean disappearance or defeat; rather, it allows the self to participate more fully in the world’s constant movement. Identity becomes fluid and relational, formed through contact with other beings, objects, sensations, and rhythms.

The poem therefore presents perception as a creative act. Careful attention reveals connections within what initially seems random or fragmented. Repetition becomes rhythm, coincidence becomes pattern, and noise becomes music. Meaning is not imposed on reality from outside, nor is it found in a single final explanation. It emerges through the act of listening, noticing, and remaining open to change.

Ultimately, the poem imagines liberation as the abandonment of an isolated individual center. The self becomes most alive when it accepts its place within an unstable but interconnected world. Through its flowing language and shifting sensory associations, the poem suggests that reality’s chaos need not be mastered to become meaningful. When approached with openness and attention, that chaos can be experienced as harmony: an ongoing composition in which consciousness, nature, language, and perception all participate.
outputs.L5:
Surrounded by the hush of cedar and pine, I watched a Blackburnian warbler flare through the branches like a living ember. Its orange throat caught the morning light, bright against the deep green shadows.

For days, I had fought the silence of the forest, filling it with restless thoughts and unanswered questions. But beneath that tiny bird’s song, resistance felt useless.

I chose to surrender—not to fear or defeat, but to the quiet truth that some things cannot be controlled. Surrounded by wings, wind, and awakening light, I finally let the world be enough.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single-paragraph surreal prose poem about surrendering to one’s surroundings, using dense internal rhyme, repetition, wordplay, and vivid natural imagery.
counterfactuals.output: I loosen my name in the rain, let each letter gutter and glitter down the fern’s green throat; no longer I, but eye, but dew, but the blue bruise of distance dissolving. The pines lean in, needling their hymns through my skin, and I listen, I glisten, I lessen—bone by stone, breath by moss-soft breath—until the hill wears my heartbeat like a buried drum. Below, the river unravels its silver riddle: give in, give in, be given; so I wade where the current is currently everything, where minnows flicker like loose thoughts and roots write dark scripts in the silt. Wind winds me into its wild alphabet. Clouds crowd my mouth with milk-white thunder. I taste the dusk, its plum and bloom, its violet violence, and surrender is no fall but a flowering: my hands become branches, my veins rain, my shadow sheds me. Night nests in my chest; stars start there, small sparks in the bark. I am not lost, not found—I am ground, I am sound, I am the round world rounding me, and I yield, I field, I become what beholds me.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an experimental stream-of-consciousness poem beginning with “Surrounded by bone” and spiraling outward through cells, trees, people, animals, color, wind, and music.
counterfactuals.output:
Surrounded by bone  
I begin where the marrow murmurs—  
red workshop, white weather,  
a small republic of cells  
dividing their silence into more silence,  
into skin, into touch, into the thought  
that touch is a door left breathing.

And outward—

the cells remember leaves,  
their green machinery turning light  
into sugar, shadow, rings;  
trees lift their many-fingered questions  
through soil-dark centuries,  
roots exchanging rumors with rain.

Outward—

people pass beneath them,  
coat-open, heart-open, shut as windows,  
each face carrying a crowd of faces,  
each name a cup trembling  
with what cannot be named.

A dog follows the bright grammar of scent.  
A crow punctuates the roof.  
Horses translate distance into thunder.  
Moths orbit a pale mistake.  
The whale, far below,  
sings one blue corridor into another.

Blue—then yellow—then the red  
behind the eyelids,  
colors spilling beyond their borders:  
violet tasting of iron,  
green ringing like glass,  
orange warm with forgotten kitchens.

And the wind enters everything  
without becoming anything—  
turning pages, turning weathercocks,  
turning my breath inside out  
until the trees are lungs,  
the people are branches,  
the animals are moving notes,

and music—

music unbuttons the air,  
a drum in the blood,  
a wire of violin drawn through dusk,  
piano rain, brass sunlight,  
the low animal hum of the earth  
spinning beneath every voice.

I spiral farther, farther—  
bone to cell,  
cell to leaf,  
leaf to hand,  
hand to wing,  
wing to color,  
color to wind,  
wind to song—

until the song surrounds the bone  
and the bone, listening,  
becomes no boundary at all.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a maximalist prose poem centered on the phrase “Surrender in the center to surroundings.” Include recursive language, near-rhymes, alliteration, and dreamlike transformations.
counterfactuals.output:
**Surrender in the Center to Surroundings**

At midnight the mirrors molt. Their silver skins slip soundlessly across the floor, becoming rivers, becoming ribbons, becoming roads that remember the feet that have not yet walked them. In the room within the room within the room, a small red clock eats its own hands and asks the hour, asks the hour asking the hour, until time is only a thyme-scented animal asleep beneath the tongue. I enter by exiting. I awaken deeper into the dream.

**Surrender in the center to surroundings.**

The sentence circles itself like a serpent made of soft consonants, like a prayer wearing the weather’s feathers. Surrender: render, re-enter, return. Center: scent there, sent where, the tender terror of a point pretending not to be a portal. Surroundings: round rings, ground wings, the world whorled around a word. Say it and the ceiling becomes a sea; say it again and the sea becomes a ceiling crowded with chandeliers of jellyfish, each blue bell tolling without sound, each tentacle writing your name in an alphabet of ache and echo.

I stand at the center, but the center stands inside me. Inside me, another I stands at another center; inside that I, another room blooms; inside that room, a child made of candlelight holds a miniature moon; inside the moon, an old moth dreams it is the child dreaming it is me. We exchange faces as easily as flowers exchange fragrance. My eyes become doors. My doors become deer. The deer leap through a forest of forks, each silver tine trembling with a possible path. Left is leaf. Right is night. Straight ahead bends backward.

**Surrender in the center to surroundings.**

Around me, the walls whisper and widen. Wallpaper roses release their roots, rooting through plaster, past laughter, into the black loam of lost afternoons. The staircase grows gills and swims upward. The windows unfasten from the house and flock south, bright panes beating against the dusk. A wardrobe opens its wooden mouth and exhales winter: white weather, wet feathers, snow slow as sorrow. In every flake a smaller house; in every house a smaller storm; in every storm, myself repeating: surrender, soft-render, soul-renter—until the words blur into birds.

Then the surroundings enter me: mountains migrate into my molars; thunder nests under my ribs; cities flicker along my nerves, their taxis tiny yellow thoughts swerving toward dawn. The desert pours its hourglasses into my blood. The ocean occupies my left ear and argues with the orchard in my right. Apples rise like red planets; whales drift through their cores, singing low, slow, below language. I am no longer surrounded. I am the surrounding, the ring around the ring, the rumor around the room.

And still the center recedes, a seed inside a seed, a secret seating itself deeper in the dark. I pursue it by becoming still. I hold still until stillness holds me. I listen until listening becomes a labyrinth, and at its heart is an ear, and in that ear is a labyrinth, and at its heart is an ear listening to me listen. What it hears is not silence but silk, not silk but silt, not silt but the soft collapse of distance.

**Surrender in the center to surroundings.**

Now gravity grows generous. Down drifts upward; up pours under. My shadow sheds me and strolls away wearing my oldest grief like a velvet coat. My grief becomes a green moth. The moth becomes a mouth. The mouth opens, and out flies the room within the room within the room, carrying the child, the clock, the candle-moon. They orbit my astonishment. They hum: home, foam, phantom; center, splinter, enter; surrender, surround, resound.

I dissolve without disappearing. My hands become handfuls of rain. My bones branch into birches, pale and patient. From my skull sprouts a stairway, and on each step sleeps a different sky. I climb downward through them: saffron sky, submarine sky, sky full of keys, sky stitched from eyelids, sky where every star is a scar learning to shine. At the final step waits the first step. At the first step waits the foot that has not yet fallen.

So I fall.

So I flower.

So the flower falls through me.

At last—if at last can exist in a dream devouring its own beginning—the center opens like an eye and reveals no throne, no stone, no solitary flame, but everything leaning into everything: dust dazzling dust, breath borrowing breath, the near and the nowhere nesting together. The world is not a wheel with a hub but a hush with innumerable mouths. Each mouth speaks the same impossible instruction, each voice strange and mine:

**Surrender in the center to surroundings.**

And the surroundings answer by becoming the center.

And the center answers by surrendering.

And surrender, surrounded by surrender, begins again.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an incantatory, psychedelic passage in which boundaries between the body and the environment dissolve. Mention bees, skeletons of trees, popcorn, a blue planet, a black-and-white cow, and a Blackburnian bird.
counterfactuals.output:
Come, bees, stitch your golden static through my blood.  
Come, skeletons of trees, unlock your antlered fingers inside my lungs.  
I breathe out bark; the forest breathes me in.

Popcorn moons burst white behind my eyes—  
small edible galaxies, salted with thunder—  
while far below, or deep within, a blue planet  
turns like a cool pearl in the mouth of darkness.

A black-and-white cow walks through my ribs,  
grazing the green echoes of my name.  
Her bell rings once, and my bones become rivers;  
it rings twice, and every stone remembers milk.

Then the Blackburnian bird—ember-throated,  
bright as a match struck in a dream—  
flies from the hollow of my chest  
into the blazing leaves, though there are no leaves,  
only feathers, only skin, only sky  
forgetting which of us is which.

Bees, carry me.  
Trees, wear me.  
Cow, dream me beneath your slow, cloud-colored breath.  
Blue planet, roll through my open skull.

I am the hive and the honey-dark air.  
I am the root drinking my own footsteps.  
I am popcorn, star, hoof, wing, and rain—  
and the world is my body  
opening everywhere at once.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Gertrude Stein–influenced prose poem about being surrounded, blending sonic association, puns, repetition, surreal imagery, and long tumbling sentences.
counterfactuals.output:
**A Round of Around**

Surrounded, she said, and the sound rounded her, round as a room without corners, though every corner wore a little crown and every crown was counting, one corner, two corner, cornucopia, corn in the ear, an ear in the wall listening to the wallpaper whisper paper paper paper as if paper were a pale parade passing through a pair of doors that had forgotten how to be apart.

Around her were chairs sitting seriously in other chairs, were spoons spooning moonlight from the blue bowl of noon, were clocks with their hands in their pockets, tick and tuck, tick and tuck, sewing the hour into a coat too close to close, and she wore it because wearing is where-ing, because to wear a thing is to ask where it ends and where you begin, and where, where, where went the small brass bird that had been nesting in the question mark.

She was surrounded by the near and the nearly, by the dear and the dearly departed commas, by a flock of locks and a key that kept saying quay, quay, as if the sea were a sentence docking inside her, salt syllables climbing the stairs, wave after wave after waiver, until even the ceiling became a feeling and lowered its white face to say you are under me, you are understood, you are standing under the standing.

But surrounded is not surrendered, no, a round is not an end unless the end bends, unless the bend becomes a ribbon and the ribbon remembers it was once a road, and on that road seven red umbrellas walked without rain, each carrying beneath it a small dry storm, each storm named Rose though none was a rose, though all were rising.

Closer came the cups, closer came the cupboards, closer came the hush with its plush little shoes, and everything touched without touching, everything crowded politely, the lamps, the lambs, the letters that had escaped from envelopes and now grazed on the carpet, B beside bee beside be, being being being, until she could not tell whether she was inside the room or the room was inside the ringing of her name.

So she stood still, which is another way of moving among what moves around you, and said round, and said sound, and said surround, and the word made a door of itself, then another door, then another, all opening inward, all opening outward, all opening into a garden where the hedges held hands and the paths went everywhere together.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
